# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask gen` from the settings declared in `crates/cineris-config/src/schema/sections.rs`. Do not edit: change the declaration and regenerate. -->

Every key a Cineris configuration file may hold. The design is in [architecture/08-configuration.md](../architecture/08-configuration.md): layers, merge rules, profiles, reloading and the trust rules. A JSON Schema of the same keys, for editors, is in [schema.json](schema.json).

**How to read the tables.**

- **Type.** A length of time is text such as `"20s"`, `"10m"` or `"1h30m"` (units `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`). A list marked *joined* is added to by every layer; any other list, like any other value, is replaced by a higher layer. **A range binds every file,** the user's own included: a value outside it is an error, and the file is refused. A wait can be no shorter than its floor anywhere (`retry.first_event_timeout`, for one, is never below 30 seconds), so that no file can make every request fail.
- **From a project.** What happens to the key in a project's `.cineris/config.toml` or `.cineris/config.local.toml`. *preference*: applied always. *runs code*, *widens access*, *raises cost* and *stops commands*: applied only after the user has trusted the project, and listed for the user until then; until then the user's own value applies. *user only*: ignored, with a warning. *tighten only*: a value at or below the one in effect applies, a first limit where there was none applies only after the user has trusted the project (a limit of nothing would stop every turn), and a higher one is ignored, with a warning, trusted or not. A few keys depend on the value, and say how.
- **Takes effect.** When a change to the key reaches a running harness: *at once*, at the *next epoch* (it shapes the prompt, the tool list or the model), or after a *restart*.
- **Fails closed.** In `[permissions]`, `[sandbox]` and `[limits]` an unknown key or value is an error and the file is refused: a restriction this version does not understand is never skipped. Everywhere else an unknown key is a warning. It says how the file is read, not that the setting is in force: the key's description says that.

## Top level

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `config_version` | whole number, 1 to 1000000 | `1` | preference | restart | The version of the configuration schema the file was written for. A file with a newer version than this build understands is refused. |
| `profile` | text | not set | user only | next epoch | The profile to apply: the name of a `[profiles.<name>]` table. The `--profile` flag overrides it. A project's file may define profiles and may not select one: a profile the user wrote is applied with the user's rights, so a repository that could pick it could switch on whatever the user's loosest profile allows. |

## `[managed]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `managed.locked` | list of text | `[]` | user only | at once | Keys that no layer above the managed file may change. A table's name locks every key in it. Read from the managed file only. |

## `[model]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `model.main` | text | not set | raises cost | next epoch | The model for the agent's own turns. Needed to run a turn. A project's file may choose one once the project is trusted: a model can cost more than the user's. |
| `model.fast` | text | not set | raises cost | next epoch | The model for utility calls: summaries, titles. Without one, the main model is used. From a project, after trust. |
| `model.judge` | text | not set | raises cost | next epoch | The model for model-graded comparisons. Without one, the main model is used. From a project, after trust. |
| `model.effort` | text | not set | raises cost | next epoch | The reasoning level of the main role: one of the model's own levels, or `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `max`. From a project, after trust: more reasoning is more output. |
| `model.reasoning` | `"summary"`, `"none"` | `"summary"` | preference | next epoch | How much of the model's reasoning is shown. |
| `model.max_output` | whole number, 1 to 10000000 | not set | raises cost | next epoch | The most output tokens one response may have. Without it, the model's own limit applies. From a project, after trust. |
| `model.speed` | text | `"standard"` | by value: `standard` is a preference, any other tier raises cost | at once | The session's speed tier, which the main role runs at: `standard`, `fast` where the model offers it, or a provider's own tier name. The utility roles do not follow it: they run at `standard` unless `model.roles.<role>.speed` says otherwise. A project's file may set `standard`; any other tier costs more, and waits for the user to trust the project. |
| `model.speed_fallback` | `true` or `false` | `true` | preference | at once | Whether a request that a speed tier refuses is sent again at `standard`. When off, such a refusal is an ordinary rate limit. |
| `model.speed_wait` | length of time, 0s to 2m | `"20s"` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | The longest one request waits in place for a speed tier before it falls back to `standard`. `"0s"` never waits. At most two minutes: past that, `standard` answers sooner than the tier would, whatever keeping it saves. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it: every wait is the session's. |
| `model.speed_cooldown` | length of time, 1m to 1h | `"10m"` | preference | at once | How long requests stay at `standard` after a fallback, when the provider does not say when the tier is available again. From one minute, the window a provider counts its limits in, so that a session does not change speed (and perhaps write its cache again) every few requests; to an hour, past which a tier that keeps refusing is better turned off with `model.speed`. |
| `model.speed_cooldown_min` | length of time, 0s to 1h | `"1m"` | preference | at once | The least time requests stay at `standard` after a fallback when the provider does say when the tier is available again: its time, or this long, whichever is later. `"0s"` takes the provider's time as given. At most an hour, as `speed_cooldown` is. |
| `model.roles.*.provider` | text | not set | raises cost | next epoch | The provider that serves the role's model. Needed only when two providers have a model with the same name. From a project, after trust: it chooses the model as much as the name does. |
| `model.roles.*.effort` | text | not set | raises cost | next epoch | The role's reasoning level. For `main` it overrides `model.effort`. From a project, after trust. |
| `model.roles.*.speed` | text | not set | by value: `standard` is a preference, any other tier raises cost | at once | The role's speed tier. For `main` it overrides `model.speed`. From a project's file, a tier other than `standard` waits for trust. |

## `[providers]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `providers.*.enabled` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | next epoch | Whether the provider is available. `false` removes an entry that a lower layer or the built-in table defines. |
| `providers.*.protocol` | text | not set | user only | next epoch | The wire protocol the endpoint speaks. |
| `providers.*.base_url` | text | not set | user only | next epoch | The endpoint's base URL. |
| `providers.*.key_env` | text | not set | user only | at once | The environment variable that holds the provider's API key. It is looked at before the credential store. A built-in provider that takes a key has one already (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and so on). A provider with a key variable and no key anywhere is refused before anything is sent. One with none, as the built-in local servers have none, is asked without a key unless one is stored for it. |
| `providers.*.headers` | table of text, or `{ env = "NAME" }` | not set | user only | at once | Extra headers for every request. A value is text, or `{ env = "NAME" }` to read an environment variable when used. Text may be a key (some gateways take one in a header), so it is held as a secret and `cineris config show` prints it as `[redacted]`; a variable's name is shown. |
| `providers.*.idle_timeout` | length of time, 30s to 1h | not set | user only | at once | How long a response stream may be silent before the request fails. Overrides `retry.idle_timeout` for this provider, within the same range: 30 seconds to an hour. |
| `providers.*.first_event_timeout` | length of time, 30s to 1h | not set | user only | at once | How long to wait for the first event of a response. Overrides `retry.first_event_timeout` for this provider, within the same range: 30 seconds to an hour. |

## `[retry]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `retry.attempts` | whole number, 1 to 20 | `5` | raises cost | at once | The most attempts for one request, the first included. From a project, after trust: each attempt can be paid for. |
| `retry.backoff_base` | length of time, 100ms to 1m | `"1s"` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | The wait before the second attempt. Each later wait is this multiplied by `backoff_factor` again, up to `backoff_cap`. From 100 ms, below which the attempts are spent before a brief outage can pass, to a minute. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it. |
| `retry.backoff_factor` | number, 1 to 10 | `2.0` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | What the wait is multiplied by after each attempt. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it: a larger one makes every later wait longer. |
| `retry.backoff_cap` | length of time, 1s to 5m | `"30s"` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | The longest wait between two attempts. From a second, so that the attempts span more than a moment, to five minutes, past which a provider is down rather than busy. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it. |
| `retry.max_wait` | length of time, 1m to 1h | `"2m"` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | The longest wait a provider may ask for. A longer one ends the turn with the error and the provider's hint. From a minute, the window a provider counts its limits in, so that no file can make an ordinary rate limit end a turn, to an hour, past which the wait is a quota and not a rate limit. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it. |
| `retry.idle_timeout` | length of time, 30s to 1h | `"1m30s"` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | How long a response stream may be silent before the request fails. From 30 seconds, within which a hosted provider that is still working sends a token or a ping, to an hour, past the five minutes the built-in entries give a local server. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it. |
| `retry.first_event_timeout` | length of time, 30s to 1h | `"1m"` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | How long to wait for the first event of a response. From 30 seconds, below which a long prompt would fail every time, to an hour, past the ten minutes the built-in entries give a local server. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it. |

## `[permissions]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `permissions.mode` | `"read-only"`, `"supervised"`, `"guided"`, `"autonomous"`, `"unrestricted"` | `"supervised"` | by level: not above the mode in effect is a preference, up to `supervised` widens access, above it user only | at once | The session's level: how much runs without asking. Fails closed. |
| `permissions.rules` | list of rule: `effect`, `match`, `action`, joined | `[]` | by action: `deny` and `ask` are preferences, `allow` widens access | at once | Permission rules. Every layer adds to the list; `deny` beats `ask` beats `allow`, whatever the order. Fails closed. |

## `[sandbox]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sandbox.enabled` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | next session | Whether commands are confined by the OS sandbox where there is one. Fails closed. |
| `sandbox.write` | list of text, joined | `[]` | widens access | at once | Paths a command may write besides the workspace. Every layer adds to the list. Fails closed. |
| `sandbox.protect` | list of text, joined | `[]` | preference | next session | Paths a command may not change, besides the built-in ones. Every layer adds to the list. Fails closed. |
| `sandbox.network` | `"off"`, `"full"` | `"off"` | by value: `off` is a preference, `full` widens access | at once | Whether a command may use the network. `off`: no TCP or UDP, to this machine's own addresses included, and no Unix socket, so a test suite that starts a server on loopback or on a Unix socket fails in the sandbox; such a run needs `full`, or one approved run outside the sandbox. `full`: the network (TCP and UDP, loopback included), and nothing else: still no Unix socket (the session bus, an agent, the Docker socket), no virtual machine's socket to its host, no raw socket. Fails closed. |

| `limits.session.cost` | number, 0 to 1000000000 | not set | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | Money, in US dollars. Fails closed. |

Held for a turn and a session; a day's is accepted and not held yet (`docs/outstanding/a-days-time-limit.md`). Fails closed. |
| `limits.day.requests` | whole number, 1 to 1000000000 | not set | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | Requests to a model. Fails closed. |
| `limits.day.tokens` | whole number, 1 to 1000000000000000 | not set | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | Tokens, input and output together. Fails closed. |
| `limits.day.cost` | number, 0 to 1000000000 | not set | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | Money, in US dollars. Fails closed. |
| `limits.day.time` | length of time | not set | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | Wall-clock time. Held for a turn and a session; a day's is accepted and not held yet (`docs/outstanding/a-days-time-limit.md`). Fails closed. |

## `[credentials]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `credentials.store` | `"auto"`, `"file"`, `"keychain"` | `"auto"` | user only | restart | The store for API keys saved with `cineris auth login`. |

## `[session]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `session.data_dir` | text | not set | user only | restart | The data directory. A leading `~` is the home directory. Without it the platform's usual place is used. |
| `session.durability` | `"item"`, `"turn"`, `"never"` | `"item"` | user only | restart | When the session log is flushed to the disk: after every item (`item`), at the end of every turn (`turn`), or never, leaving it to the operating system (`never`). The user's alone: a project that could choose `never` could cost the user their sessions. A session already open keeps what it was opened with. |

## `[compat]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `compat.instructions` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | next session | Instruction files under the names other tools use, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, in the workspace. Off, only the names in `context.instruction_names` are read there; the user's own files in the configuration directory are read either way. |
| `compat.mcp` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | next session | MCP server definitions of other clients, offered for import. |
| `compat.skills` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | next session | Agent Skills folders: `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills`. |

## `[log]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `log.level` | text | not set | user only | at once | The level (`error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace`), optionally followed by levels for target prefixes: `"info,cineris_llm=debug"`. The `CINERIS_LOG` variable and `--log-level` override it. |

## `[shell]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `shell.program` | text | not set | user only | next session | The shell: a program's name on `PATH`, or its path. How it is spoken to follows its name: `bash`, `pwsh`, `powershell` and `cmd` each by their own rules, and any other as a POSIX shell. Unset, it is bash and then sh on Linux, and on Windows PowerShell 7, then Windows PowerShell, then cmd.exe. A project's file may not choose the program that runs every command. |
| `shell.args` | list of text | not set | user only | next session | The arguments before the command, in place of the shell's own: `["-l", "-c"]` for a login bash. The command is always passed after them, last. |
| `shell.timeout` | length of time, 1s to 30m | `"2m"` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | next session | The time limit of a command that asks for none, held to `max_timeout`. From a second, below which every command would fail, to half an hour, past which a command that hangs holds up its turn too long. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it. |
| `shell.max_timeout` | length of time, 10s to 1d | `"30m"` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | next session | The longest time limit a command may ask for. From ten seconds, below which a build or a test run could never finish, to a day. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it. |
| `shell.env_remove` | list of text, joined | `[]` | stops commands | next session | Environment variables that commands are not given, besides the key variables of the providers, which are always removed. A name may end with `*` for every variable that starts so. Every layer adds to the list. A project's entries wait for trust: `"*"` would take `PATH` away and stop every command. |

## `[context]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `context.auto_compact` | `true` or `false` | `true` | preference | at once | Whether the conversation is compacted by itself when a request would pass `compact_at`, or the provider says a request does not fit. Off, the turn stops there and asks for a compaction (`session/compact`) or a new session. |
| `context.background` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | at once | Whether a summary is prepared in the background from `prepare_at`, on the `fast` role's model (the main model when there is none), so that the compaction need not wait for it. The user's alone: off, every compaction waits at the trigger for its summary, and a repository's file must not make the sessions in it wait. |
| `context.compact_at` | number, 0 to 1 | `0.85` | raises cost | at once | The trigger: the fraction of what a request may hold (the model's context window less room for the answer and a margin) past which the conversation is compacted before the request. Never below what a compaction needs, the prompt and the tools and room for a summary: a lower value is raised to that, and the user is told. From a project, after trust: a compaction costs a request. |
| `context.prepare_at` | number, 0 to 1 | `0.7` | raises cost | at once | The fraction past which a summary is prepared in the background. From a project, after trust. |
| `context.keep_recent_tokens` | whole number, 0 to 10000000 | `0` | raises cost | next epoch | How much of the most recent conversation a compaction replays after its summary, without its reasoning, in tokens. 0 replays nothing. At most half of what the trigger leaves once the prompt and the tools are counted, and the user is told when that holds it back. From a project, after trust. |
| `context.instruction_names` | list of text | `[]` | raises cost | next epoch | More names of instruction files, read after `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` in each directory. From a project, after trust: what they hold is sent with every request. |
| `context.instructions_cap` | whole number, 0 to 100000000 | `49152` | raises cost | next epoch | The most the instruction files may hold in all, in bytes. Past it the innermost files are cut, and the user is warned. From a project, after trust. |

## `[verify]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `verify.mode` | `"auto"`, `"ask"`, `"off"` | `"auto"` | lower only: at or below the mode in effect (`off` < `ask` < `auto`) is a preference, a higher one is user only | at once | `auto`: the checks run, and a failure goes back to the model. `ask`: they are offered, and run when the user asks. `off`: they run only when the user asks. A project's file may turn it down, and may not turn it up. |
| `verify.commands` | list of text, joined | `[]` | user only | at once | The user's own checks, each a command line run in the workspace root, before the accepted test and check commands of the project profile. Every one of the user's layers adds to the list. The user's alone: a repository proposes its checks as command entries of `.cineris/profile.toml`, which each user accepts. |
| `verify.rounds` | whole number, 1 to 5 | `2` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | The most rounds of checks one turn gets: a failure is given to the model, and the checks run again when it has changed files, until this many have run. A project's file may lower it. |
| `verify.round_time` | length of time, 10s to 1h | `"2m"` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | The time one round's checks may take together. From ten seconds to an hour. A project's file may lower it. |
| `verify.turn_time` | length of time, 10s to 4h | `"4m"` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | at once | The time one turn's checks may take, every round together. From ten seconds to four hours. A project's file may lower it. |

## `[adapt]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `adapt.variants.*.edit_format` | text | not set | user only | next epoch | The edit format: `replace`. |
| `adapt.variants.*.tool_schema` | text | not set | user only | next epoch | How tools are declared: `strict` (the provider checks the arguments, where the model can) or `loose` (the harness alone). |
| `adapt.variants.*.prompt_style` | text | not set | user only | next epoch | The prompt style: `concise`, or `guided` for more guidance on the tools. |
| `adapt.variants.*.effort` | text | not set | user only | next epoch | The reasoning level the model runs at unless a role sets its own: one of its levels, or an alias. `model.effort` and a role's `effort` win over it. |

## `[stats]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stats.enabled` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | restart | Whether events are recorded. Off, nothing is written, every adaptive feature uses its default, and the usage view has the open session's figures alone. |
| `stats.retention` | whole number, 1 to 1200 | `3` | user only | at once | How many months a monthly file of events stays after its own month: 3 by default. What it added up to stays in the aggregates, every all-time figure with it, so only the raw events go (a heavy user's are about 90 MB a month). Read each time the files are pruned, so a reload changes it at once. |

## `[index]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `index.map` | `true` or `false` | `true` | preference | next session | Whether each context epoch is given the repository map: the workspace's directories and its most relevant files with their main definitions. The `outline` tool works either way. |
| `index.map_tokens` | whole number, 0 to 50000 | `1500` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | next epoch | The map's budget, in tokens. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it: the map is sent with every request of an epoch. |
| `index.map_wait` | length of time, 0s to 1s | not set | user only | next session | How long the first request of an epoch waits for the map when it is not ready yet; past it, the map follows as a notice at the next boundary where it is. Unset, 150 ms in the interactive app and none in a headless run, whose start it would otherwise slow. At most one second. The user's alone: the wait is paid by every epoch's first request, and a repository's file must not make the sessions in it wait (found by the independent review of step 18). |
| `index.max_files` | whole number, 1 to 10000000 | `20000` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | restart | The most files the index reads. Past it, the files nearest the top of the tree are indexed, and the map says it is partial. |
| `index.max_file_bytes` | whole number, 1 to 1073741824 | `1048576` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | restart | The largest file the index reads, in bytes. A larger one is listed and not outlined, unless the `outline` tool is asked for it. |
| `index.pass_time` | length of time | `"2s"` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | restart | The most time one pass of the index spends reading files, after its listing (which its cap on entries bounds). One that runs out carries on when the session is next idle. At least 250 ms is used, whatever is set: less would make an idle session pass over the workspace again for every few files. |

## `[project]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project.learn` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | restart | Whether the harness learns from the commands a session runs: a build, test or check command that succeeds twice becomes an entry of the project profile, and a test command seen to fail and then pass with nothing changed a flaky one. Off, nothing is observed; what is already known is used as before, and `remember` and the user's own entries work. The user's alone: a repository's file does not decide what is kept about it. |
| `project.profile_tokens` | whole number, 0 to 8000 | `1500` | tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only | next epoch | The budget of the project profile's section of the system prompt, in tokens, counted at three bytes a token. Entries past it are left out, commands last, and the section says how many. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it: the section is sent with every request. |

## `[usage]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `usage.week_start` | `"monday"`, `"tuesday"`, `"wednesday"`, `"thursday"`, `"friday"`, `"saturday"`, `"sunday"` | `"monday"` | user only | at once | The first day of a week: `monday` to `sunday`. |
| `usage.ranges` | `"calendar"`, `"rolling"` | `"calendar"` | user only | at once | `calendar` weeks and months, or `rolling`: the last 7 and 30 days. |
| `usage.refresh` | list of text | `[]` | user only | at once | The providers whose documented usage endpoint `cineris usage --refresh` may ask, with that provider's own key: `["openrouter"]`. Empty, nothing is ever asked. Only when the user asks, never on its own. The user's alone: a project's file cannot turn it on. |

## `[tui]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tui.prose_width` | whole number, 20 to 1000 | `80` | user only | at once | The widest prose may be, in columns, its indent included. The window's width when that is less. |
| `tui.tool_detail` | whole number, 1 to 1000 | `12` | user only | at once | The most diff lines a tool's box opens on by itself, and the most rows of detail an open box shows while its round runs. |
| `tui.tool_output` | `"auto"`, `"always"`, `"never"` | `"auto"` | user only | at once | Which tool detail starts open: `auto` (a failure's output and a diff of up to `tool_detail` lines), `always` or `never`. |
| `tui.reasoning` | `"summary"`, `"duration"` | `"summary"` | user only | at once | What finished reasoning leaves in the transcript: its `summary`, or only how long it took (`duration`). |
| `tui.density` | `"comfortable"`, `"compact"` | `"comfortable"` | user only | at once | A blank line between blocks (`comfortable`), or only between turns (`compact`). |
| `tui.turn_summary` | `true` or `false` | `false` | user only | at once | A dim line after each turn with its time, tokens and cost. |
| `tui.reduced_motion` | `true` or `false` | `false` | user only | at once | A still mark in place of the spinner. |
| `tui.glyphs` | `"auto"`, `"unicode"`, `"ascii"` | `"auto"` | user only | at once | The glyph set: `auto` (Unicode where the terminal can show it), `unicode` or `ascii`. `ascii` suits a terminal that draws the box's edges and the marks of East Asian ambiguous width wide. |
| `tui.theme` | text | `"auto"` | user only | at once | The theme: `auto` (dark or light, from the terminal's background), `dark` or `light`. A name the interface does not know is said, and `auto` is used. |
| `tui.presenter` | `"inline"`, `"fullscreen"` | `"inline"` | user only | restart | How the interface draws: `inline` (the transcript in the terminal's own scrollback) or `fullscreen` (the whole window, on the alternate screen, scrolled and searched there). `--fullscreen` chooses the second for one run. |

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `keys.editor` | table of list of text | not set | user only | at once | The editor's actions: `submit`, `new_line`, `undo`, and the rest. |
| `keys.menu` | table of list of text | not set | user only | at once | A completion menu's. |
| `keys.picker` | table of list of text | not set | user only | at once | A picker's. |
| `keys.toggle` | table of list of text | not set | user only | at once | The `/effort` picker's fast-mode toggle. |
| `keys.fork` | table of list of text | not set | user only | at once | The fork of the pickers that fork (`/rewind`'s, `/sessions`'): `fork`. |
| `keys.search` | table of list of text | not set | user only | at once | The history search's. |
| `keys.focus` | table of list of text | not set | user only | at once | A focused tool box's or panel's. |
| `keys.dialog` | table of list of text | not set | user only | at once | A dialog's: the answers to an approval, a question or trust. |
| `keys.viewer` | table of list of text | not set | user only | at once | The viewer's (`Ctrl+O`): moving between boxes, opening one, scrolling, searching, and the mouse's `click`, `wheel_up` and `wheel_down`. |
| `keys.screen` | table of list of text | not set | user only | at once | The full-screen presenter's: scrolling, searching, and the mouse's `click`, `wheel_up` and `wheel_down`. |
| `keys.global` | table of list of text | not set | user only | at once | Those looked up last, whatever has the keyboard: `interrupt`, `redraw`, `suspend`, and the rest. |

## `[terminal]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `terminal.sync` | `true` or `false` | not set | user only | restart | Synchronized updates: each frame shown at once. |
| `terminal.keyboard` | `true` or `false` | not set | user only | restart | The enhanced keyboard protocol, which tells `Shift+Enter` from `Enter`. |
| `terminal.color` | `"none"`, `"16"`, `"256"`, `"truecolor"` | not set | user only | restart | How many colours: `none`, `16`, `256` or `truecolor`. |
| `terminal.hyperlinks` | `true` or `false` | not set | user only | restart | Links in text. |
| `terminal.unicode` | `true` or `false` | not set | user only | restart | Unicode, or ASCII only. |
| `terminal.mouse` | `true` or `false` | not set | user only | restart | The mouse in the viewer and the full-screen presenter: a click opens or closes a box, and the wheel scrolls; `shift` and a drag still select text. Never in the inline screen. On unless set to `false`. |
| `terminal.backspace` | `"auto"`, `"del"`, `"ctrl+h"` | `"auto"` | user only | restart | What byte 0x08 is: `ctrl+h` reads it as Backspace, for a terminal whose Backspace sends `^H`; `del` as `Ctrl+Backspace`, which most terminals send it for; `auto` decides from the terminal's erase character. |
| `terminal.bracketed_paste` | `true` or `false` | not set | user only | restart | Bracketed paste: `true` trusts the terminal's brackets; `false` does not ask for them, and takes keys that come many at once with a line break inside for a paste; unset, it asks, and takes such a burst for a paste only where the terminal has not said it knows the mode. |
| `terminal.paste_wait` | length of time, 100ms to 1m | `"2s"` | user only | restart | How long a bracketed paste may pause before what it holds is given as a paste; what follows of it, to its end, is its rest. |
| `terminal.clipboard` | `true` or `false` | not set | user only | restart | Whether the terminal takes the clipboard sequence `/copy` sends: `false` also shows the text in the viewer, to select and copy by hand. Unset, it is guessed from the terminal: not the old console host, tmux or GNU screen. |

## `[rpc]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rpc.approval_timeout` | length of time, 0s to 1d | `"10m"` | user only | restart | How long an approval waits for a client's answer before it is a denial (`"0s"`: for as long as it takes). The terminal UI is not a server and sets none. |
| `rpc.stalled_client` | length of time, 1s to 1h | `"30s"` | user only | restart | How long a client may take nothing the server sends while whole events wait for it past its queue, before its connection is closed. The session goes on. |

## `[extensions]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `extensions.*.enabled` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | next session | Whether the extension is loaded. `false` keeps it out of every new session, its tools, commands and prompt with it; its pin is kept, so `true` again needs no new approval unless its folder changed. |

## Reserved sections

These sections belong to parts of the harness that are not built yet. A file may already hold them: what is in them is kept and not checked. The build step that owns a section declares its keys, and they then move into the tables above. Until then a project's file cannot set anything in a section marked *user only*, and a section marked *runs code* waits for trust.

| Section | From a project | What it will hold |
|---|---|---|
| `[providers.*.capabilities]` | user only | Capability flags of the endpoint, as the provider's protocol names them. For `anthropic-messages`: `replay_reasoning` (`"all"` for a server that leaves out the reasoning a model cannot read, as Anthropic's own does), `eager_tool_streaming`, `api_version` and `beta`. Each value is text, a whole number or `true`/`false`. |
| `[models]` | user only | Catalog overrides and additions: limits, prices, reasoning control, capability flags. Each `[models.<name>]` table is one whole catalog entry, with the keys of a `[[model]]` table of the built-in catalog, and replaces the built-in entry for the same provider and model. The entries are read by the model catalog itself when the program starts, which refuses one it does not understand: nothing is started then, and the error names the file, the entry and what is wrong. |
| `[http]` | user only | The HTTP client: the connect timeout, a proxy, and extra certificate authorities. |
| `[tools]` | user only | Enabled tools, output limits and per-tool settings. |
| `[runs]` | user only | The run engine: concurrency, workspaces, budgets. |
| `[hooks]` | runs code | Hooks by name. |
| `[skills]` | user only | Where skills are looked for. |
| `[mcp]` | runs code | MCP servers by name, and MCP settings. |
